subject.title: Org claim: vmware-aiops + vmware-monitor — @kingaiwork lookalikes impersonate @zw008 listings (same pattern as #2966/#3035)

question: Should staff confirm and hide the two named lookalike listings, and does the repeated @kingaiwork pattern justify account-level enforcement beyond those resources?
rationale: The public evidence supports urgent listing review, but production audit data and the disruptive scope of account enforcement are available only to authorized moderators or admins.

options.title: Hide both and review account
options.body: Confirm both reports, hide the two owner-qualified listings, and inspect the publisher catalog and prior enforcement history for proportionate account action.

options.title: Hide only the listings
options.body: Resolve the immediate collisions while deferring account-level action unless additional catalog evidence is recorded.

options.title: Request more evidence
options.body: Leave the resources unchanged only if staff cannot verify the copied content, misleading identity, or collision impact from production data.

recommendation.title: Hide both and review account
recommendation.body: Confirm both reports, hide the two owner-qualified listings, and inspect the publisher catalog and prior enforcement history for proportionate account action.

likelyOwner.reason: Among the history-backed candidates, this person has the broadest adjacent registry moderation and release context for a decision that may extend from two listings to account-level enforcement.
